record.original_question: A Mersenne number has the form M_n = 2^n - 1, and a Mersenne prime is a Mersenne number that is prime. Are there infinitely many Mersenne primes?

evidence.quote: For every positive integer n, the nth Mersenne number is defined by M_n=2^n-1. A Mersenne number which is prime is known as a Mersenne prime.
Hence, there remain several open problems about Mersenne primes: Is the number of Mersenne primes infinite?

artifact.self_contained_problem: For every positive integer $n$, define the $n$-th Mersenne number by $M_n = 2^n - 1$. A Mersenne number that is a prime in $\mathbb{Z}$ is called a Mersenne prime. Determine whether the set $\{n \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0} : M_n \text{ is prime}\}$ is infinite; equivalently, prove or disprove that there exist infinitely many Mersenne primes.
artifact.status_search_result: The infinitude of Mersenne primes is a long-standing open conjecture in number theory. As of 2026, only 52 Mersenne primes are known (the most recent being M_136279841, discovered in October 2024 by GIMPS), and no proof of infinitude exists.

status_evidence.title: Mersenne prime - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: It is not known whether there are infinitely many Mersenne primes.
status_evidence.claim: The infinitude of Mersenne primes remains an open conjecture.

status_evidence.title: GIMPS - Great Internet Mersenne Prime Search
status_evidence.snippet: M136279841 is the 52nd known Mersenne prime, discovered October 2024.
status_evidence.claim: Only finitely many Mersenne primes are currently known; the question of infinitude is unresolved.
